### Fixed

Escaped the unescaped apostrophe by changing `I'm` to `I&apos;m` in the JSX text.

```24:28:/Users/arronlinton/Desktop/lab/personal-site/src/components/Template/SideBar.js
      <p>
        Hi, I&apos;m Arron. I&apos;m a New York City based Software Engineer,
        Solutions Engineer, and Rutgers University Alumni.
        <a href="https://www.rutgers.edu/">{}</a>.
      </p>
```

### Verified

`src/components/Template/SideBar.js` now reports **no linter errors**.

### Why this fixes it

JSX lints (like `react/no-unescaped-entities`) warn on raw `'` in text nodes; using `&apos;` is the recommended escape.

From your `package.json`, this is a **Create React App** app (`react-scripts`). Typical flow:

### Run locally (development)

```bash
cd /path/to/personal-site
npm install
npm start
```

That runs `react-scripts start` and opens the dev server (usually `http://localhost:3000`).

**Node:** `package.json` expects **Node `>= 20.x`**.

### Other useful scripts

| Command | What it does |
|--------|----------------|
| `npm run build` | Production build → `build/` |
| `npm test` | Runs Jest (`npx jest`) |
| `npm run lint` | ESLint on `**/*.js` |
| `npm run lint:fix` | ESLint with `--fix` |
| `npm run deploy` | `predeploy` (build + `react-snap`) then `gh-pages -d build` |
| `npm run analyze` | Build + bundle size explorer |

For day-to-day work, **`npm install`** then **`npm start`** is what you need.

Few updates (perform each implementation 1 at a time in the exact order for dependencies reasons):
1 — DESIGN SYSTEM

Set up a dark-themed design system using CSS variables. Background: #0B0F19. Primary text: #E8E6E0. Accent green: #1EB482. Accent blue: #1E78FF. Use 'Playfair Display' for display headings and 'DM Sans' for body text. Import both from Google Fonts. Add a subtle grid overlay (3% white, 60px cells) as a background texture.

2 — NAV

Build a sticky navbar with 'ARRON J. LINTON' in DM Sans 500 on the left. Right side: nav links About, Resume, Projects, Contact in 13px with 0.08em letter-spacing. Add a green dot badge that reads 'Open to opportunities'. Nav background should be semi-transparent dark (#0B0F19 at 85% opacity) with a 1px bottom border at 8% white. Animate in on load with a fade down.

3 — HERO LAYOUT

Create a two-column hero section. Left column (55%): headline, subheadline, role tags, CTA buttons, social icons. Right column (45%): profile photo in a hexagonal clip-path frame with a glowing green border. Add a large decorative background number '01' in Playfair Display at 20vw, 4% opacity, positioned behind the right column.

4 — HEADLINE

The main headline reads: "I bridge the gap between technical complexity and business outcomes." Set in Playfair Display, 52px, font-weight 700, line-height 1.15. The word 'bridge' should use the accent green color (#1EB482). Animate in with a staggered word-by-word fade-up (50ms delay per word) on page load.

5 — ROLE TAGS

Below the headline, add a subheadline in DM Sans 300, 18px: "Full-stack engineer and solutions architect who turns product vision into scalable, AI-powered systems." Then add three pill tags: 'Solutions Engineer', 'Software Engineer', 'Founder @ Magistri Dev'. Pill style: 1px solid border at 20% white, 6px/16px padding, 13px DM Sans, transparent background with 5% white on hover.

6 — CTA BUTTONS

Two CTA buttons side by side. Primary: 'View My Work' — solid green (#1EB482) background, dark text, 12px/24px padding, no border-radius (sharp corners). Secondary: 'Download Resume' — transparent background, 1px white border at 40% opacity, white text. On hover, primary darkens 10%; secondary fills with 8% white. Both have a subtle 200ms ease transition.

7 — SOCIAL ICONS

Add a row of icon links below the buttons: GitHub, LinkedIn, Dribbble (or personal site), Email. Use SVG icons at 18px, color #888, hover color #1EB482 with a 150ms transition. Space them 20px apart. Add a thin vertical divider line before the row using a 1px white border at 10% opacity.

8 — STATS BAR

Below the hero, add a full-width stats strip with a top border (1px, 8% white). Three stats evenly spaced: '10+ Projects Delivered', '5 Years Experience', '100% Client Satisfaction'. Stat numbers in Playfair Display 36px, labels in DM Sans 12px uppercase with letter-spacing. Add a subtle count-up animation (0 to final value over 1.2s) triggered when the section enters the viewport using IntersectionObserver.

9 — PHOTO FRAME

The profile photo should sit inside a hexagonal clip-path container. Add a glowing border using a pseudo-element with a green (#1EB482) gradient stroke at 60% opacity and a subtle box-shadow: 0 0 40px rgba(30,180,130,0.2). The hex frame should have a slow rotating animation (360deg over 20s, linear, infinite) on the border glow only — not the photo itself.

10 — RESPONSIVE

Make the layout fully responsive. At ≤768px: stack columns vertically, photo first, text below. Reduce headline to 36px. Stack CTA buttons full-width. Reduce stats bar to a 1-column grid. Ensure nav collapses to a hamburger menu with a slide-down drawer. All animations should still fire on mobile.

### 1 — Design system

- Wired fonts in `public/index.html`: **Playfair Display** + **DM Sans** (with `preconnect`), set `theme-color` to `#0B0F19`, kept the legacy font link for other pages.
- Imported the design system in `src/static/css/main.scss` after `typography`.

### 2 — Nav
- Added `src/static/css/components/_site-header.scss` and `@import` in `main.scss`.
- Updated `Navigation.js`: `#header` + `site-header`, brand, **“Open to opportunities”** pill with green dot, nav links in a `site-header__right` group.
- Sticky bar: **85% `#0B0F19`**, blur, **1px bottom** at **8% white**, **fade-down** on load.
- **Hamburger.js**: optional `menuClassName`, dark drawer styles, menu offset under the bar; fixed `className` bug on menu items (`index-li`).
- **≥769px**: show links, hide burger; **undo** the old theme rule that hid `.links` below 980px for `#header.site-header` only. **≤768px**: hide links, show burger.

### 3–10 — Hero, headline, tags, CTAs, social, stats, photo, responsive
- **`Index.js`**: 55% / 45% hero (grid in CSS), new headline + sublead + pill tags + CTAs + `HomeSocialRow` + hex photo + `HomeStats`.
- **`HomeSocialRow.js`**: GitHub, LinkedIn, **personal site** (root `PUBLIC_URL`), Email — **18px SVGs**, **#888 → #1EB482** in **150ms**, **20px** gaps, **vertical rule** at **10% white** before icons.
- **`HomeStats.js`**: Full-width strip, **Playfair 36px** numbers, **DM Sans 12px** uppercase labels, **IntersectionObserver** + **1.2s** count-up (with `easeOutCubic`).
- **`_index.scss`**: Full layout: staggered **word fade-up** (50ms steps), **“bridge”** in green, pills, sharp green / bordered secondary buttons (**200ms**), **“01”** deco (**20vw**, **4%**), hex **clip-path**, **rotating conic glow** only on `.home__hexGlow`, green glow shadow; **≤768px**: column stack, **photo first**, **36px** headline, **full-width** CTAs, **1-column** stats.

**Note:** The mobile menu is still **react-burger-menu’s slide panel** (from the right), styled dark and tucked under the header—not a custom top “sheet” animation. If you want a true slide-down panel, that would need a different menu implementation or heavier overrides.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The issue is clear: `@include breakpoint(large)` applies 3 columns when the viewport width is up to 1280px, since the `large` breakpoint in skel is defined as `"(max-width: 1280px)"`. The naming convention for breakpoints in skel can be counterintuitive: `@include breakpoint(large)` activates when the viewport width is less than or equal to 1280px, meaning it applies on most desktop screens. This aligns with the definition of the `large` breakpoint as `"(max-width: 1280px)"`, where styles are applied when the screen size fits within that constraint. At wide screens like 1920px, the `large` breakpoint does not apply because `(max-width: 1280px)` evaluates to false, resulting in only the base `.projects-grid` with 1fr applying1 column. On narrower screens like 400px, the `large` breakpoint applies, causing 3 columns to be used instead. This leads to an inverted layout where wide desktops get 1 column and narrower screens get 3 columns, which is the opposite of typical expectations. The user sees three narrow columns because they are viewing on a laptop with a viewport width of 1280px or less. To fix this, remove the `@include breakpoint(large)` block that applies 3 columns and instead use a single column layout. Also, remove any redundant `@include breakpoint(small)` overrides. For sizing, update `.projects-grid__devices` to have a responsive width using `max-width: min(42rem, 100%)` or `width: 100%; max-width: 48rem;` and increase its height proportionally to maintain aspect ratio, preventing images from being squashed on larger screens. Use `aspect-ratio: 16 / 10` or `min-height: 14rem` with `height: auto` for `.projects-grid__devices` to maintain proper sizing. For desktop layouts with absolutely positioned children, set `position: relative` on the parent and ensure a defined height.
</details></think>

### What was wrong

In `_projects.scss`, **`@include breakpoint(large)`** uses the theme’s **`max-width: 1280px`** query. So on most laptops and tablets the grid became **3 columns**, each column got only ~⅓ of the width, and the fixed **13rem** device stack looked tiny.

### What we changed

- **Always one column**: Removed the `breakpoint(large)` block that set `grid-template-columns: repeat(3, …)`.
- **Full-width row cards**: `.projects-grid__item` / `.projects-grid__link` use **`width: 100%`** with a **`max-width: min(52rem, 100%)`** so each project is one centered row that can grow on large screens.
- **Larger previews**: `.projects-grid__devices` is **`width: 100%`**, **`aspect-ratio: 2 / 1`**, with **`min-height: clamp(14rem, 42vw, 22rem)`** and a **`max-height`** cap. The **desktop** image uses **`object-fit: cover`** so it fills that area instead of shrinking to a strip.
- **Mobile tweak** (`breakpoint(small)`): Slightly adjusted phone/tablet widths so the stack still reads when the viewport is narrow.

You should now see **one project per row** on desktop and mobile, with a much larger device preview block per project.

_**Agent (default)**_

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

### Cause
1. **`[react-ga] gaTrackingID is required`** — In CI, `NODE_ENV` is `production` but **`REACT_APP_GA_TRACKING_ID` is unset**, so `ReactGA.initialize(undefined)` ran during **react-snap** prerender on every route.
2. **`Cannot write to stream after nil` (highland)** — Often a **react-snap / puppeteer** stream bug, sometimes worsened by noisy failures or timing during crawls. Fixing GA removes a real runtime error during crawl; **`skipThirdPartyRequests`** can also reduce flaky network work during prerender.

### Fixes (commit **`5500550`**)
- **`src/components/Template/Analytics.js`** — Only call `ReactGA.initialize` when **`NODE_ENV === 'production'`** and **`REACT_APP_GA_TRACKING_ID`** is set; use a **`useRef`** so init runs once, then `set` + `pageview` on route changes.
- **`package.json` (`reactSnap`)** — Set **`"skipThirdPartyRequests": true`** so prerender doesn’t chase third-party URLs as aggressively.
- **`.github/workflows/github-pages.yml`** — Pass **`REACT_APP_GA_TRACKING_ID: ${{ secrets.REACT_APP_GA_TRACKING_ID }}`** so you can add a repo secret later and get real GA in production builds.

### What you should do
1. **Push** and re-run the deploy (no secret required for a clean crawl).
2. **Optional:** In GitHub → **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions**, add **`REACT_APP_GA_TRACKING_ID`** (e.g. `G-XXXXXXXX` or `UA-…`) if you want analytics in the live build.

If the **highland** error still appears after this push, say so and we can try the next lever (e.g. react-snap options, splitting `build` vs `react-snap`, or swapping prerender tool).

_**Agent (default)**_

### What was failing

The stack trace points at **`inlineCss`** in **react-snap** (`inlineCss` → `page.evaluate` → **`fetch`**). With **`inlineCss: true`**, react-snap loads each page in Puppeteer and **`fetch()`es your CSS URLs** to inline them. In **GitHub Actions** that often returns **`net::ERR_FAILED` / `TypeError: Failed to fetch`**, then react-snap’s pipeline blows up with the **highland “Cannot write to stream after nil”** error (secondary to the first failure).

### What we changed

In **`package.json`** → **`reactSnap`**:

- **`"inlineCss": false`** — skips that in-browser `fetch()` path so prerender can finish in CI.

Your app still gets **normal CRA CSS** in `build/static/css/...`; you only lose the extra “inline critical CSS into HTML” optimization from react-snap.

### Commit

**`e27e980`** — `fix react-snap CI: set inlineCss false for GitHub Actions`

Push `main` and the deploy step should get past `react-snap`. If anything else fails, paste the new log.
